name: Byron Donalds / Brian Avila
pollingDetails: Pollsmax average of 37 polls (Oct 2026): Donalds 48.1%, Jolly 43.0%. Individual October polls range from a tie to +11: St. Pete Polls Oct 5-7 (836 LV) 45-45; UNF Oct 12-19 (1,471 LV, ±2.8) 49-47; RedBox Research Oct 20-23 (4,832 LV) 49-44; co/efficient (R) Oct 18-20 49-40; Stetson Oct 1-9 52-41; Mason-Dixon/NBC6 Sep 28-Oct 1 (625 LV) 48-41.
raised: ~$168.8M ($18.0M campaign + $150.8M Friends of Byron Donalds PC; PC has $34.3M available; FL Div. of Elections data through Oct 25 2026 per Sparkers Soapbox). Florida Politics (Oct 17, through Oct 9): >$146M raised, >$110M spent.
backers: Republican Party of Florida ($2.8M in-kind), GEO Group ($1M), Fighting for Florida's Families PC ($1M), Republican Governors Association, data-center and real-estate donors, Florida Chamber of Commerce, Florida Realtors PAC, NFIB, 36 sheriffs
lgbtqDetails: HRC Congressional Scorecard 0% (117th Congress); voted against the Respect for Marriage Act (2022, Washington Post vote tally) and the Equality Act (2021); as a FL House member in 2020 co-filed bills to preempt local LGBTQ protections and penalize doctors providing transition care to minors (Wikipedia). Running mate Bryan Avila voted Yea on SB 254 (2023 gender-affirming care ban, FL Senate roll call May 4 2023). Equality Florida Action PAC's Jolly endorsement criticized Donalds for 'targeting transgender people.'
platform: U.S. Rep. for FL-19 (Naples) since 2021, former FL House member (2016-2020), ex-banker raised in Brooklyn; would be Florida's first Black governor. Runs on continuing the DeSantis/Trump agenda: eliminating homestead property taxes (backs Amendment 3), property-insurance 'reform' through more competition, strict immigration enforcement, school choice, expanding data centers, and opposition to climate regulation. Running mate Bryan Avila is a Hialeah state senator (2022-2026) and former House member.
controversy: Wikipedia/AP: 1997 marijuana charge (diverted) and 2000 no-contest felony theft plea (later expunged); 2024 Jim Crow remarks drew national backlash; Campaign Legal Center ethics complaint over 100+ undisclosed stock trades (2024); Florida Bulldog reported inaccurate congressional financial disclosures and charter-school contracts tied to his wife's firms. Collier School Board member Kelly Mason filed a second assault lawsuit in July 2026 (he calls it political). WLRN found a Donalds attack ad deceptively edited a Jolly clip on gender-affirming care. Ran 'Convenience' and 'This Is Florida' ads calling Jolly a 'fraud' for changing positions (Florida Politics).
endorsements: Donald Trump, Ron DeSantis (Sept 3 2026), Sens. Rick Scott, Ashley Moody, Ted Cruz, Speaker Mike Johnson, Elon Musk, Florida Chamber of Commerce, Florida Realtors PAC, NFIB, Florida PBA, Everglades Trust, 36 sheriffs, John Morgan, incoming legislative leaders Jim Boyd and Sam Garrison
primaryResult: won Aug 18 REP primary 47.8% (810,552 votes) over Jay Collins 25.2%, James Fishback 10.5%, Paul Renner 8.5% in an 11-way field

name: David Jolly / Gwen Graham
pollingDetails: Pollsmax average (Oct 2026): Jolly 43.0% vs Donalds 48.1%. Jolly tied or led only in St. Pete Polls Oct 5-7 (45-45) and Democratic-sponsored Change Research polls (47-47 Oct 8-10); UNF Oct 12-19 had him within the margin at 47-49; most other October polls show him down 5 to 11.
raised: ~$26.0M ($12.7M campaign incl. $3.1M state matching funds + $13.3M Florida 2026 PC; PC has $971k available; FL Div. of Elections data through Oct 25 2026 per Sparkers Soapbox). Florida Politics (Oct 17, through Oct 9): ~$21M raised, >$17M spent. DGA added $1M on Oct 20 (Florida Phoenix).
backers: Florida Democratic Party, Democratic Governors Association ($1M), National Education Association ($250k), AFSCME ($200k), Florida Education Association, Florida AFL-CIO, state public matching funds, Bill Clinton fundraiser (>$3M)
lgbtqDetails: Endorsed by Equality Florida Action PAC (Aug 14 2026), which cited his 2014 support for marriage equality, his 2016 bipartisan NDAA effort to protect LGBTQ workplace nondiscrimination, his defense of parents' access to health care for transgender children, and opposition to book bans; also endorsed by the Florida Democratic Party LGBTQ+ Caucus and Dolphin Democrats. Per Wikipedia he opposes transgender women in women's sports but would not repeal the existing law. No HRC endorsement was found in searches.
platform: Former Republican U.S. Rep. for Pinellas-based FL-13 (2014-2017), later MSNBC commentator, independent, Forward Party member, and Democrat since April 2025. Campaign centers on affordability: a state-backed catastrophic property-insurance fund, a one-year moratorium on hyperscale data centers, a 10-year education plan with a 30% teacher raise, codifying Roe, an assault-weapons ban, and a proposed Office of Civil Rights in the Governor's Office. Running mate Gwen Graham is a former U.S. Rep. (FL-2), 2018 gubernatorial runner-up, and Biden-era Assistant Secretary of Education.
controversy: Declined all general-election debates with Donalds, citing Donalds' 'repeated lies' (WCTV, Sept 21 2026), which Donalds' ads call a 'debate dodge' (Florida Politics). Donalds brands his party switch and position changes on abortion and guns as fraudulent (Florida Politics). His 2016 Senate campaign admitted editing his Wikipedia page to remove Scientology and lobbying references (Wikipedia). Publicly told national Democrats 'I'm begging for help' to close the cash gap (Florida Politics, Oct 2026).
endorsements: Barack Obama (Oct 24 2026), Bill Clinton, Hakeem Jeffries, Equality Florida Action PAC, Florida AFL-CIO, Florida Education Association, AFSCME Florida, Sierra Club Florida, Forward Party, Florida Rights Restoration Coalition, Miami Herald, Tampa Bay Times, Orlando Sentinel, Palm Beach Post, Daniella Levine Cava, Donna Shalala, Alex Sink
primaryResult: won Aug 18 DEM primary 61.0% (761,558 votes) over Dayna Foster 15.1% and Dotie Joseph 9.6%

name: Scott Eckhard Jewett / Nicole Skelly
pollingDetails: Not broken out in any public poll; October surveys lump third-party and NPA candidates into 'other' at roughly 1-4%. Libertarian gubernatorial nominees in Florida historically draw under 2%.
raised: ~$14,000 (WLRN/Florida Public Media, Oct 22 2026; FL Div. of Elections data)
backers: Libertarian Party of Florida, small individual donors
lgbtqDetails: No votes or statements on LGBTQ+ issues found; the LPF describes his platform as 'socially liberal, fiscally conservative' but he has not addressed LGBTQ+ policy specifically.
platform: Boca Raton entrepreneur and first-time candidate running a self-styled 'Libertarian 2.0' campaign. Platform: restructure Florida's insurance regulatory system to bring back private insurers, eliminate property taxes on homestead residences, cut taxes and regulations, remove Flock license-plate cameras, require data centers to 'do no harm,' expand nuclear energy including thorium, and strict immigration enforcement including penalties for employers hiring undocumented workers. Participated in the Florida Public Media voter guide.

name: Charles Burkett / Ruben A. Coto
pollingDetails: Not broken out in any public poll; grouped with 'other' candidates at 1-4% in October surveys.
lgbtqDetails: No public record on LGBTQ+ issues found.
platform: Four-term mayor of Surfside (Miami-Dade), including during the 2021 Champlain Towers South collapse that killed 98 people. Originally filed as a Republican, then announced an NPA run in May 2026. Platform: affordability, fixing property and auto insurance, stopping the 'Manhattanization' of South Florida; told the Florida Public Media voter guide he supports no abortion restrictions at any stage. Running mate Ruben A. Coto has no reported public profile.
controversy: WLRN reported nearly all of his campaign social media is AI-generated, featuring an AI 'avatar' of himself, which he defends as a way to compete with better-funded rivals.

name: Frank J. Russo / Rachel Rodriguez
pollingDetails: Not broken out in independent public polls. A campaign-distributed press release claimed a poll showing him at 7.1%; that figure is self-reported and not from a recognized pollster.
raised: ~$860,000 (WLRN/Florida Public Media, Oct 22 2026; FL Div. of Elections data), the best-funded of the minor candidates
backers: Largely self-funded and individual donors (per WLRN)
lgbtqDetails: No public record on LGBTQ+ issues found.
platform: Businessman who left the Republican Party for independent status in 2022 and qualified as NPA in June 2026. Platform: affordability, child protections, raising average teacher pay to $75,000, and welcoming state investment in AI and data centers (unlike most other candidates). Campaigns heavily via Instagram video. Running mate Rachel Rodriguez ran in the Aug 18 Republican gubernatorial primary, receiving 1.6%. Did not participate in the Florida Public Media voter guide.

name: Moliere "Moe" Dimanche / Benjiman Rojas
pollingDetails: Not broken out in any public poll.
lgbtqDetails: No public record on LGBTQ+ issues found.
platform: Orlando-area author who ran for Orlando mayor in 2023 but was disqualified for unpaid fees. Platform: abolish homeowners associations, audit the DeSantis administration, make home buying easier, and support e-scooters for students. Participated in the Florida Public Media voter guide; known for tongue-in-cheek social media videos.
controversy: WLRN reported he served prison time for grand theft until 2016 and that state campaign-finance records show he is appealing fines from this election; his 2023 Orlando mayoral bid was disqualified for not paying qualifying fees.

name: Dean Ocean Abrams / Joe Van Vactor
pollingDetails: Not broken out in any public poll.
lgbtqDetails: No public record on LGBTQ+ issues found.
platform: Switched from Republican to NPA in 2022. Affordability-focused platform: no property taxes on homesteaded properties worth up to twice the county median, and opposition to data centers. Campaigns mostly through online influencer interviews; did not participate in the Florida Public Media voter guide.
controversy: WLRN noted an Instagram video in which he claimed data centers could become military sites used to launch drones.

name: Jeffrey Peter "Dr. Jeff" Datto / Juan Santana
pollingDetails: Not broken out in any public poll.
lgbtqDetails: No public record on LGBTQ+ issues found.
platform: Hialeah resident and former Miami VA spinal-cord-injury research associate (BallotReady). Has no campaign website or published platform; campaigns through high-energy social media videos. Did not participate in the Florida Public Media voter guide. WLRN reported he has not voted in Florida since 2020.
controversy: WLRN, citing the Palm Beach County Civics Scorecard, reported a 15-plus-year pattern of pro se civil-rights and disability-discrimination lawsuits filed by Datto across multiple states, and videos of him arguing with police.

name: Kathy Anderson / Daniel Nokovich
pollingDetails: Write-in candidate; name does not appear on the printed ballot and is not included in any poll.
lgbtqDetails: No public record on LGBTQ+ issues found.
platform: Qualified write-in ticket certified by the Florida Department of State (June 2026). No campaign website, platform, or news coverage of Anderson was found. Running mate Daniel Nokovich ran in the Aug 18 Republican gubernatorial primary and received 0.3% (5,188 votes).

name: Erik Morris / LeRoy Alaways
pollingDetails: Write-in candidate; name does not appear on the printed ballot and is not included in any poll.
lgbtqDetails: No public record on LGBTQ+ issues found.
platform: Tampa resident (per AOL/USA Today Network list) who qualified as a write-in for governor; certified by the Florida Department of State with running mate LeRoy Alaways. No platform, campaign website, or substantive news coverage found.

name: James Uthmeier
pollingDetails: St. Pete Polls for Florida Politics, Oct 5-7 2026 (836 LV, ±3.4): Uthmeier 45%, Rodríguez 43%, 12% undecided. Targoz/James Madison Institute Sep 28-Oct 4 (854 LV): 50-40. Democratic-sponsored SEA Polling Oct 11-14 (805 LV) had Rodríguez up 35-34. Sabato's Crystal Ball rates the race Likely Republican.
raised: ~$15.5M ($2.0M campaign incl. $173k matching funds + $13.5M Friends of James Uthmeier PC; PC has $5.7M available; FL Div. of Elections data through Oct 25 2026 per Sparkers Soapbox)
backers: Republican Attorneys General Association (seven-figure commitment), Republican Party of Florida ($364k in-kind), Ike and Laura Perlmutter ($500k), Associated Industries of Florida, Club for Growth, Florida Sheriffs Association
lgbtqDetails: As AG he sued the American Academy of Pediatrics, WPATH and the Endocrine Society under false-advertising and racketeering laws over gender-affirming care (Dec 2025, myfloridalegal.com); sent warning letters to Miss America/Miss Florida over transgender contestants (WUSF, Apr 2026) and to Irish dance organizations over gender-identity policies (WFLA, June 2026); demanded Gainesville PD rescind a gender-expression detainee-search policy (WCJB, July 2026); and celebrated the 11th Circuit's Aug 2026 ruling upholding Florida's drag-show law (LGBTQ Nation).
platform: Destin native, Georgetown Law graduate, former Trump 2016 campaign counsel and DeSantis general counsel, chief of staff and 2024 presidential campaign manager; appointed AG in Feb 2025 when Ashley Moody went to the U.S. Senate. Priorities: prosecuting child predators, aggressive immigration enforcement (helped create 'Alligator Alcatraz'), a unit targeting China-linked companies, and Big Tech/AI child-safety suits against Discord and OpenAI.
controversy: Held in civil contempt by U.S. District Judge Kathleen Williams in June 2025 for telling police they could keep enforcing a blocked immigration law (Florida Phoenix). A leaked Leon County grand jury report said $10M from a Medicaid settlement was 'misappropriated' via Hope Florida while he was chief of staff; it found insufficient evidence to charge him and an appeals court ordered findings struck, but Rodríguez's ads call him 'the root of corruption' (WUSF, Oct 23 2026). Also drew coverage for subpoenaing Anthony Fauci and sending a demand letter to The New York Times (Sparkers Soapbox summary).
endorsements: Donald Trump, Ron DeSantis, Republican Party of Florida, Republican Attorneys General Association, Club for Growth, Associated Industries of Florida, Florida Sheriffs Association and 51 county sheriffs

name: Jose Javier Rodriguez
pollingDetails: St. Pete Polls Oct 5-7 2026 (836 LV, ±3.4): Rodríguez 43%, Uthmeier 45%. Targoz/James Madison Institute Sep 28-Oct 4: 40-50. His campaign-aligned SEA Polling survey Oct 11-14 showed him ahead 35-34 with a large undecided share; Change Research (D) Sep 7-9 had a 46-46 tie.
raised: ~$3.8M ($1.7M campaign incl. $361k state matching funds + $2.1M Floridians for JJR PC; PC has $99k available; FL Div. of Elections data through Oct 25 2026 per Sparkers Soapbox). Launched a 'multimillion-dollar' statewide ad buy in Oct (Florida Politics).
backers: Florida Democratic Party ($360k in-kind), Florida AFL-CIO, SEIU Florida, AFSCME Florida, Florida Professional Firefighters, UNITE HERE, Latino Victory Fund, End Citizens United, VoteWater, SAVE Action PAC, state public matching funds
lgbtqDetails: Endorsed by Equality Florida Action PAC (statewide slate, list updated Oct 16 2026), SAVE Action PAC (Miami's LGBTQ advocacy PAC) and the Dolphin Democrats. As a Miami Democratic legislator (2012-2020) he was part of the caucus that backed LGBTQ nondiscrimination measures; no anti-LGBTQ votes found.
platform: Miami native, Brown and Harvard Law graduate, Peace Corps volunteer, Florida House (2012-2016) and Senate (2016-2020), then Biden's Assistant Secretary of Labor for Employment and Training. Runs as 'the people's lawyer': rein in utility rate hikes and hidden fees, prosecute corporate-landlord price gouging, recover Hope Florida money, scrutinize Alligator Alcatraz contracts, protect public lands and education funds, and defend abortion access and gun-safety laws.
controversy: Lost his 2020 Senate seat by 34 votes after a 'ghost candidate' sharing his surname was secretly funded in a scheme that sent former Sen. Frank Artiles to jail; news investigations tied the dark money to FPL-linked consultants (WUSF, Miami Herald). Rodríguez was the victim, not a participant. The Republican Party of Florida sued to block a Democratic Hope Florida ad attacking Uthmeier, then dropped the suit (WUSF).
endorsements: Equality Florida Action PAC, Florida AFL-CIO, SEIU Florida, AFSCME Florida, Florida Professional Firefighters, Latino Victory Fund, End Citizens United, former AG Bob Butterworth, Alex Sink, Bill Nelson, Kathy Castor, Maxwell Frost, Gwen Graham, Dave Aronberg, Miami Herald, Orlando Sentinel, Sun Sentinel, Palm Beach Post

name: Blaise Ingoglia
pollingDetails: The closest Cabinet race. St. Pete Polls Oct 5-7 2026 (836 LV, ±3.4): Ingoglia 44%, Taddeo 42%, 14% undecided. Targoz/James Madison Institute Sep 28-Oct 4 (853 LV): tied 43-43. Change Research (D) Sep 7-9: tied 44-44. SEA Polling (D) Sep 7-13: tied 42-42. Florida Politics calls it a 'dead heat' across four polls.
raised: ~$14.0M ($1.78M campaign + $12.2M via Friends of Blaise Ingoglia and Government Gone Wild PACs; PCs have $1.8M available; plus $1.35M in-kind, 98% from RPOF; FL Div. of Elections data through Oct 25 2026 per Sparkers Soapbox)
backers: Republican Party of Florida ($1.35M in-kind consulting/staff), Associated Industries of Florida, Florida Professional Firefighters, Florida FOP, Florida PBA, Gun Owners of America, homebuilder and insurance-industry donors
lgbtqDetails: Voted Yea on final passage of SB 254 (2023), the ban on gender-affirming care for minors, per the Florida Senate roll call of May 4 2023 (26-13). Served in the Florida House 2014-2022 during passage of HB 1557 ('Don't Say Gay'); as RPOF chair (2015-2019) he led the party that championed those measures. No pro-LGBTQ record found.
platform: Spring Hill homebuilder (Hartland Homes), former Republican Party of Florida chair, Florida House (2014-2022) and Senate (2022-2025); appointed CFO by DeSantis in July 2025 after Jimmy Patronis left for Congress. Runs on his 'Florida DOGE' audits of local governments, eliminating homestead property taxes (backs Amendment 3), fines against slow-paying insurers, and a record $847M in unclaimed property returned.
controversy: Florida Bulldog (Aug 16 2026) reported his Form 6 financial disclosure omits 100+ properties worth ~$10M held through four Hartland LLCs; his office says the form is accurate. County leaders in Broward, Orange and Seminole disputed his DOGE 'wasteful spending' figures and he subpoenaed Orange County over DEI records (Orlando Weekly, WPTV). His office sent armed agents to a Vietnam veteran who mailed him a critical postcard (Wikipedia, Oct 2025). Taddeo's Oct 2026 AI-assisted 'corruption' ad ties him to the Hope Florida vote; a Political Cortadito fact-check found it did not show personal involvement.
endorsements: Ron DeSantis, Ashley Moody, former CFOs Jimmy Patronis, Jeff Atwater and Tom Gallagher, Republican Party of Florida, Associated Industries of Florida, Florida Professional Firefighters, Florida FOP, Florida PBA, Gun Owners of America, 62 sheriffs, Reps. Bilirakis, Bean, Cammack, Haridopolos, Mast
primaryResult: won Aug 18 REP primary 61.3% (967,504 votes) over Frank Collige 38.7%

name: Annette Taddeo
pollingDetails: St. Pete Polls Oct 5-7 2026 (836 LV, ±3.4): Taddeo 42%, Ingoglia 44%. Targoz/James Madison Institute Sep 28-Oct 4: tied 43-43 among likely voters. Change Research (D) Sep 7-9 and SEA (D) Sep 7-13 also tied. A Ruth's List poll in April had her narrowly ahead 39-38. Democrats view this as their best statewide pickup chance.
raised: ~$814k ($304k campaign incl. $74k state matching funds + $510k Friends of Annette Taddeo PC; PC has $69k available; FL Div. of Elections data through Oct 25 2026 per Sparkers Soapbox). Outspent roughly 9-to-1 (Florida Politics).
backers: Florida AFL-CIO, SEIU Florida, AFSCME Florida, CWA, Teamsters Joint Council 75, United Teachers of Dade, Ruth's List Florida, Equality Florida Action PAC, Florida Hispanic Chamber PAC, state public matching funds
lgbtqDetails: Voted Nay on HB 1557 ('Don't Say Gay') on the Senate floor March 8 2022 (roll call). Endorsed by Equality Florida Action PAC, whose director Joe Saunders cited her opposition to the Parental Rights in Education law and her work on conversion-therapy bans and nondiscrimination statutes (Florida Politics, Aug 2026).
platform: Colombian-born founder of LanguageSpeak translation company; flipped a Miami-Dade state Senate seat in 2017 and served until 2022; first Latina Democrat in the Florida Senate; 2014 Lt. Gov. nominee with Charlie Crist. Platform: an insurance-company report card on claims handling within 100 days, 'consumer champions' on the Citizens board, teams to help hurricane victims contest claims, auditing emergency spending starting with the $1.2B Alligator Alcatraz, supports larger homestead exemptions but opposes Amendment 3 as lacking guardrails.
controversy: Record of electoral losses (2008 and 2022 U.S. House, 2010 county commission, 2024 Miami-Dade clerk) is a GOP talking point (WLRN). Her AI-assisted October ad accusing Ingoglia of corruption over Hope Florida was found by Political Cortadito not to establish his personal involvement. Her profane July response to Ingoglia's 'Unapologetic' ad drew coverage (The Floridian).
endorsements: Equality Florida Action PAC, Ruth's List Florida, Florida AFL-CIO, SEIU Florida, AFSCME, Teamsters, Alex Sink, Donna Shalala, Daniella Levine Cava, Jerry Demings, Fentrice Driskell, Miami Herald, Orlando Sentinel, Sun Sentinel, Palm Beach Post, Miami Times
primaryResult: won Aug 18 DEM primary 65.6% (795,964 votes) over Earle Ford 34.4%

name: Wilton Simpson
pollingDetails: Only one public general-election poll: Targoz Market Research for the James Madison Institute, Sep 28-Oct 4 2026 (847 LV): Simpson 50%, Atkins 39%, 8% undecided (45-36 among 1,171 RV, ±2.77). He won in 2022 with 59.3% and has a roughly 500-to-1 money edge.
raised: ~$48.4M ($1.4M campaign + $47.0M across Friends of Wilton Simpson, Florida Green PAC, Future Florida and Home Grown PAC; PCs have $22.0M available; FL Div. of Elections data through Oct 25 2026 per Sparkers Soapbox)
backers: Florida Farm Bureau PAC, Florida Citrus Mutual, Florida Cattlemen's Association past presidents, Florida Chamber of Commerce, Associated Industries of Florida, Florida Forestry Association, U.S. Sugar and agribusiness donors, Florida Professional Firefighters
lgbtqDetails: As Senate President he presided over and voted Yea on HB 1557, the Parental Rights in Education ('Don't Say Gay') law, on March 8 2022 (Senate roll call 22-17). No pro-LGBTQ record found.
platform: Fifth-generation Floridian and Pasco County egg farmer; Florida Senate 2012-2022, Senate President 2020-2022; elected Agriculture Commissioner in 2022. Touts a 243% increase in farmland preserved through the Rural and Family Lands program (250,000 acres), the state fluoride and lab-grown meat bans, a law barring 'foreign countries of concern' from buying farmland, clearing the concealed-weapon license backlog, and excused absences for 4-H/FFA students.
controversy: Publicly feuded with Gov. DeSantis in January 2025 over immigration-enforcement legislation before DeSantis endorsed his reelection (Wikipedia, Sparkers Soapbox). Declined repeated invitations to appear on WLRN's The Florida Roundup (WLRN, Oct 2026). A Sparkers Soapbox analysis noted three of his committees raised $23.9M but spent only ~$645k, mostly on taxes, raising questions about the war chest's purpose. Primary rival Matt Taylor attacked him over aerial spraying (Lake Okeechobee News).
endorsements: Donald Trump, Ron DeSantis, Ashley Moody, Rick Scott, 61 of 67 sheriffs, Florida Farm Bureau PAC, Florida Citrus Mutual, Florida Chamber of Commerce, Associated Industries of Florida, Florida Professional Firefighters, Miami Herald, Palm Beach Post
primaryResult: won Aug 18 REP primary 68.9% (1,110,689 votes) over Matt 'the Welder' Taylor 31.1%

name: Joey Mendoza Atkins
pollingDetails: Targoz/James Madison Institute, Sep 28-Oct 4 2026 (847 LV): Atkins 39%, Simpson 50%. No other public poll. Runs a shoestring campaign against a well-funded incumbent who won by 19 points in 2022.
raised: ~$91,000 (campaign account, 99% from 2,093 mostly small-dollar donors, plus an $8,000 personal loan; no political committee; FL Div. of Elections data through Oct 25 2026 per Sparkers Soapbox). Florida Politics (Aug 2026) reported $60,850 raised, $60,000 spent.
backers: Small-dollar individual donors, Florida Democratic Agricultural Caucus, Florida Alliance for Retired Americans
lgbtqDetails: No votes, statements or Equality Florida endorsement found; the Dolphin Democrats (Broward LGBTQ+ Democratic club) recommend him as part of the Democratic slate.
platform: Miami trial attorney (FAU, University of Toledo Law 2013) who did legal aid for migrant farmworkers and DACA youth, worked as a sports agent, and was the 2024 Democratic nominee in FL-26. Platform: fight food and fuel price gouging and suspend the state gas tax, a statewide moratorium on data centers, protect family farms from developers, close the 'rent-a-cow' agricultural tax loophole, and oppose federal immigration raids on farm communities.
controversy: None significant reported. (Briefly entered then withdrew from the 2026 U.S. Senate special primary before qualifying for this race.)
endorsements: Florida Democratic Agricultural Caucus, Florida Alliance for Retired Americans, Florida Veterans for Common Sense, Dolphin Democrats, Sun Sentinel editorial board
primaryResult: won Aug 18 DEM primary 60.3% (716,467 votes) over Donald Prichard 39.7%

name: Kyle "KC" Gibson
pollingDetails: Write-in candidate; name does not appear on the printed ballot and is not included in any poll.
raised: ~$900 available (Florida Politics, Aug 2026; FL Div. of Elections data)
lgbtqDetails: No public record on LGBTQ+ issues found.
platform: Fort Lauderdale resident who qualified as a write-in; Florida Politics reports he has published no platform for the office and has reported almost no money. Voters must write his name in; it is not printed on the ballot.
